claims.text: Adding a small amount of aluminum to Co-free FeNiCrMn will improve its dynamic mechanical performance.
Aluminum addition will refine the grains of FeNiCrMn.
Aluminum addition will produce solid-solution strengthening in FeNiCrMn.
The proposed structural changes will improve dislocation mobility.
The proposed intervention will reduce cracking susceptibility.
Al-modified FeNiCrMn will have a better strength–ductility balance than unmodified FeNiCrMn.
The predicted improvement applies from -200°C to 500°C.
The predicted improvement applies at strain rates from 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
There is a lack of direct experimental evidence for the effect of aluminum addition on the dynamic mechanical performance of FeNiCrMn.

contradictions.description: Solid-solution strengthening ordinarily relies on solute-induced resistance to dislocation motion, whereas the mechanism states that dislocation mobility will improve. The hypothesis does not explain how these opposing effects are reconciled.
